hints: Counting from the end is awkward because the chain only runs forwards. What fixed distance would you like to maintain between two walkers?
Exactly `n` links. Then when the leading walker reaches the end, the trailing one is `n` from the end.
To *remove* a link you need the one before it, so aim the trailing walker one link earlier - and give the leading walker an `n + 1` head start.
Removing the head has nothing in front of it. Start the trailing walker at a dummy link placed before the head, and that case disappears.
